claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy has a favorable strength–ductility balance in its solidified solid-solution state.
Severe lattice distortion is responsible for the favorable strength–ductility balance of Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The random multi-element solid solution locally distorts edge-dislocation cores.
Distortion of edge-dislocation cores makes their mobility dependent on temperature and strain rate.
The tested Co-free FeNiCrMn material is a single-phase solid solution derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Mechanical behavior should be tested systematically from room temperature to approximately 900°C.
Mechanical behavior should be tested over multiple strain rates.
Processing history and microstructure should be held constant during the temperature and strain-rate comparison.
Local compositional fluctuations and atomic-size mismatch produce distorted edge-dislocation cores with wavy line configurations.
Atomic-size fluctuations shift edge-dislocation cores away from their neutral planes.
The distorted cores increase the activation barrier for edge-dislocation glide at low temperatures and high strain rates.
The elevated glide barrier preserves high yield strength at low temperatures and high strain rates.
Elevated temperature or reduced strain rate lowers the mobility barrier and increases dislocation mobility.
Greater dislocation mobility at elevated temperature or lower strain rate enhances ductility.
At low temperature and high strain rate, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show higher yield strength and limited dislocation mobility dominated by distorted edge dislocations.
At elevated temperature or lower strain rate, Co-free FeNiCrMn will become more ductile without a significant loss of overall strength relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi has less pronounced lattice distortion than Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will show a smaller temperature and strain-rate dependence of dislocation mobility than Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The proposed mechanism applies only while FeNiCrMn remains an unprecipitated, unordered solid solution, approximately up to 900°C.
A lack of a temperature- or strain-rate-dependent change in dislocation behavior and mechanical properties, or behavior indistinguishable from CoCrFeMnNi, would falsify the mechanism.
